newsitem.title: USA: Oppenheimer Funds launches first commodities fund.
newsitem.headline: Oppenheimer Funds launches first commodities fund.

text.p: OppenheimerFunds Inc said Monday it launched the Real Asset Fund, apparently the first to invest a significant part of the portfolio in financial securities linked to commodities markets.

The fund will invest at least 65 percent of total assets in derivatives, futures contracts, options, forward contracts, swaps, investment grade bonds, money market instruments, and U.S. government securities.
According to Lipper Analytical Services, the fund would be the first if its kind to dedicate a "significant" part of the fund to securities that are backed by a commodity.

"Commodities such as livestock, grains, oil and metals can provide strong long-term returns and significant risk diversification from traditional stock and bond investments," said Russell Read, head of the Oppenheimer Real Asset Fund management team.
It will use the Goldman Sachs Commodity Index as a benchmark.
"Commodities can act as a hedge against inflation due to their correlation with rising consumer and producer prices," said Mark Anson, commodities risk manager for the fund.
"Because of this, the Fund may offer inflation protection potential from the rises in prices which would hurt other financial assets," Anson said.
At Dec 31, 1996, Oppenheimer Funds managed funds with assets of more than $62 billion in more than three million shareholder accounts.
